{"slices":[{"index":0,"name":"Sign Up","x0":133.15,"x1":277.15,"docHtml":"

Slice: Sign Up

Intent

Create a Nemeo profile for a first-time external identity without creating or managing a Nemeo password. Google is the only enabled provider for MVP. A successful signup returns an authenticated browser session and continues directly to household setup; the user does not repeat authentication.

Returning users take the alternative Authenticate slice.

UI / interaction design

  • Screen: Authentication
  • MVP copy: Continue with Google.
  • The screen does not ask the user to choose sign-up versus sign-in; the provider result determines which command is processed.

Trigger and actor

The user selects the configured provider action and completes its OIDC flow. For MVP that action is Continue with Google. Nemeo receives a validated provider result through the identity adapter.

Application API contract

  • GET /v1/auth/google/start begins the browser flow and redirects the user to Google with an opaque state/nonce protected by the identity adapter.
  • GET /v1/auth/google/callback receives the provider response, validates the state and Google result, and resolves a normalized provider identity before invoking Sign Up.
  • OAuth authorization codes, tokens, state/nonce values, client secrets, and raw Google payloads remain at the HTTP/identity-adapter boundary. They are never command fields or event facts.
  • A successful User Account Created event is followed by a revocable secure browser session and a redirect to the household setup route. Signup must not require a second authentication step.
  • Callback failures, cancelled consent, invalid state, and invalid provider results return a recoverable authentication error without recording User Account Created or issuing a session.

Domain behavior

Command

Sign Up accepts a normalized, validated provider identity result. Provider tokens, authorization codes, client secrets, and raw provider payloads remain in the identity adapter and must not cross into the domain command or event payload.

The command creates a profile only when the stable (provider, providerSubject) pair is not already linked. Session issuance is an application result after the event is durably recorded.

Event

User Account Created records the new personal profile and its external identity mapping. It does not create a household or grant household access.

Command fields

Field Rule
provider google for MVP; explicit for future providers
providerSubject Required stable Google subject; never inferred from email
verifiedEmail Verified provider email, when supplied; not an identity-linking key
displayName Optional provider display name for initial profile presentation
authenticationRequestId Required correlation/idempotency identifier

Event facts

User Account Created contains a new userId, provider and stable subject mapping, initial verified email when supplied, and creation timestamp. It contains no password, provider token, authorization code, raw provider payload, or session secret.

Scenarios

First-time Google identity creates a profile

Given a valid verified Google identity whose (provider, providerSubject) pair is not linked When the user completes Continue with Google Then Nemeo creates one profile and records User Account Created And Nemeo establishes a revocable secure browser session And the user proceeds directly to household setup

Existing identity is not signed up twice

Given a Google provider subject already linked to a Nemeo profile When the user attempts signup Then Nemeo does not create another profile And the user is directed through the existing authentication path

Matching email does not merge identities

Given an unlinked Google subject whose email matches an existing profile When the user attempts signup Then Nemeo does not create a profile or merge financial data And the user is directed to complete the existing authentication path

Invalid, cancelled, or failed provider flow

Given the configured provider cannot complete or validate the OIDC flow When the signup callback is handled Then no profile or session is created And the user receives a recoverable error

Replayed signup callback is idempotent

Given the same valid signup request is delivered more than once When Nemeo processes the replay Then provider-subject uniqueness prevents a duplicate profile And at most one User Account Created event is recorded

Invariants

  • SIGNUP-001: A (provider, providerSubject) pair maps to at most one Nemeo profile.
  • SIGNUP-002: A profile is created only from a valid, verified provider result with a stable subject.
  • SIGNUP-003: Matching email addresses are not sufficient evidence for identity linking or financial-data merging.
  • SIGNUP-004: Failed, cancelled, invalid, or rejected signup emits no event and establishes no session.
  • SIGNUP-005: No Nemeo-managed password, provider credential, raw provider payload, or session secret enters the event stream.
  • SIGNUP-006: A successful signup session is scoped to the new user; household authorization begins only after household creation.

Alternate and error flows

  • Provider-subject uniqueness conflict: do not overwrite or merge; direct the user to the existing sign-in path.
  • Database/event write failure: do not issue a browser session; retry only through an idempotent request path.
  • Session issuance failure after profile creation: surface a recoverable error and allow safe retry without creating another profile.

Read models and downstream effects

User Account Created feeds Household Setup Status, which makes the initial household setup path available. The profile alone does not create a household.

Open questions

None for MVP.

Verification notes

  • Use provider contract fixtures; never use real provider credentials in automated tests.
  • Cover first-time signup, duplicate subject, email collision, invalid/cancelled callbacks, replay, event-write failure, and session-issuance failure.
  • PostgreSQL-backed integration tests should verify uniqueness, idempotency, and absence of secrets in the event payload.
  • A critical-path browser test should verify that signup proceeds directly to household setup.
"},{"index":1,"name":"Authenticate","x0":302.15,"x1":446.15,"docHtml":"

Slice: Authenticate

Intent

Authenticate a user whose external provider subject is already linked to a Nemeo profile. Google is the only enabled provider for MVP. This is the alternative path from the same authentication screen used for signup; it is not a second step after signup.

UI / interaction design

  • Screen: Authentication
  • MVP copy: Continue with Google.
  • The screen does not ask the user to choose sign-up versus sign-in; the provider result determines which command is processed.

Trigger and actor

The user selects the configured provider action and completes its OIDC flow. For MVP that action is Continue with Google. Nemeo receives a validated provider result through the identity adapter.

Application API contract

  • GET /v1/auth/google/start begins the browser flow and redirects the user to Google with an opaque state/nonce protected by the identity adapter.
  • GET /v1/auth/google/callback receives the provider response, validates the state and Google result, and resolves a normalized provider identity before invoking Authenticate.
  • OAuth authorization codes, tokens, state/nonce values, client secrets, and raw Google payloads remain at the HTTP/identity-adapter boundary. They are never command fields or event facts.
  • A successful User Authenticated event is followed by a revocable secure browser session and a redirect to the appropriate household route. Authentication must not require a second sign-in screen.
  • Callback failures, cancelled consent, invalid state, and invalid provider results return a recoverable authentication error without recording User Authenticated or issuing a session.

Domain behavior

Command

Authenticate accepts a normalized, validated provider identity result. Provider tokens, authorization codes, client secrets, and raw provider payloads remain in the identity adapter.

The command resolves an existing identity by the stable (provider, providerSubject) pair. It does not create profiles, link identities, or merge users.

Event

User Authenticated records the successful resolution of an existing Nemeo identity. The application establishes a revocable opaque browser session after the event is durably recorded; the session secret is not part of the event stream.

Command fields

Field Rule
provider google for MVP; explicit for future providers
providerSubject Required stable Google subject; used for lookup and never inferred from email
authenticationRequestId Required correlation/idempotency identifier

Event facts

User Authenticated contains the resolved userId, provider, authentication timestamp, and correlation identifier. It contains no browser session token, provider credential, or raw provider payload.

Scenarios

Existing Google identity is authenticated

Given a valid verified Google identity whose (provider, providerSubject) pair is linked When the user completes Continue with Google Then Nemeo records User Authenticated And Nemeo establishes a new revocable secure browser session And the user proceeds to the appropriate household experience

Unknown Google subject does not create an account

Given a valid Google identity whose subject is not linked When the user completes the authentication path Then Nemeo does not create a profile And the user is directed to the signup path And no authenticated session is established by this slice

Matching email does not authorize access

Given an unlinked Google subject whose email matches an existing profile When the user attempts authentication Then Nemeo does not authenticate the unlinked identity And Nemeo does not merge or link profiles And the user receives guidance to use the already-linked Google identity

Invalid, cancelled, or failed provider flow

Given the configured provider cannot complete or validate the OIDC flow When the authentication callback is handled Then no User Authenticated event is recorded And no browser session is established And the user receives a recoverable error

Replayed authentication callback

Given the same valid authentication request is delivered more than once When Nemeo processes the replay Then the request is handled idempotently And Nemeo does not create a profile or broaden authorization

Invariants

  • AUTH-001: Authentication requires an existing exact (provider, providerSubject) mapping.
  • AUTH-002: Matching email addresses are not sufficient evidence for identity linking or access.
  • AUTH-003: Authentication never creates a profile or household.
  • AUTH-004: Failed, cancelled, invalid, or rejected authentication emits no event and establishes no session.
  • AUTH-005: No provider credential, raw provider payload, or session secret enters the event stream.
  • AUTH-006: The resulting session resolves to the same user principal used by HTTP, MCP, worker, and scheduled entry points.

Alternate and error flows

  • Provider-subject lookup failure: return a recoverable error without creating or modifying identity data.
  • Database/event write failure: do not issue a browser session; retry only through an idempotent request path.
  • Session issuance failure: surface a recoverable error and allow safe retry without changing identity mappings.

Read models and downstream effects

User Authenticated feeds Household Setup Status, which makes the initial household setup path available for a user who has not yet created a household.

Open questions

None for MVP.

Verification notes

  • Use provider contract fixtures; never use real provider credentials in automated tests.
  • Cover existing identity, unknown subject, email collision, invalid/cancelled callbacks, replay, event-write failure, and session-issuance failure.
  • PostgreSQL-backed integration tests should verify exact-subject lookup, idempotency, and absence of secrets in the event payload.
  • A critical-path browser test should verify that returning users go from Google completion to their household experience without a second authentication screen.
"},{"index":2,"name":"Create Initial Household","x0":471.15,"x1":615.15,"docHtml":"

Slice: Create Initial Household

Intent

Create the new user’s first household with a user-provided name. The authenticated user becomes the household’s root manager, and subsequent budget setup is owned by that household.

Application API contract

  • POST /v1/households accepts { "name": string } for the authenticated user.
  • The application derives the root manager from the session; the client cannot provide an owner or household ID.
  • A successful response returns the created household and manager role. Duplicate initial creation is rejected or resolved to the existing household according to the command invariants.
  • The resulting household is available through GET /v1/household.
  • The route maps to Create Initial Household; Household Created is the durable domain result.

Domain behavior

Command

Create Initial Household accepts the authenticated principal and a non-empty household name. Identity and household authorization are resolved at the application boundary; the command does not accept an arbitrary owner or household scope from the client.

Event

Household Created records the household identity, display name, and root-manager ownership.

Scenarios

Create the initial household

Given an authenticated user with no household When the user submits a valid household name Then Nemeo creates one household owned by that user And the user is assigned the root manager role And Nemeo records Household Created

Household name is required

Given an authenticated user with no household When the user submits an empty or invalid household name Then the household is not created And the user receives a validation error

User already belongs to a household

Given an authenticated user who already belongs to a household When the user submits initial household setup Then Nemeo does not create a second household And the user is directed to the existing household

Unauthenticated setup attempt

Given a request without a valid authenticated principal When the request attempts to create an initial household Then Nemeo rejects the command And no household is created

Invariants

  • A user belongs to exactly one household in MVP.
  • The initial household has exactly one root manager lifecycle owner.
  • The household name is present and valid before Household Created is recorded.
  • The client cannot choose another user as the root manager.
  • Repeating the command cannot create a second household for the same user.

Open questions

None for the MVP slice.

Verification notes

  • Cover successful creation, invalid names, duplicate submission, an existing household, and an unauthenticated request with PostgreSQL-backed integration tests at the application boundary.
  • Verify that the created household is immediately available to the next budget-setup slice and that the root-manager authorization is resolved consistently for HTTP, MCP, worker, and scheduled paths.
"},{"index":3,"name":"View Current Household","x0":640.15,"x1":784.15,"docHtml":"

Slice: View Current Household

Intent

Return the authenticated user’s current household when one exists. This is the resource read used after authentication and during onboarding; absence of a household tells the application to show initial household setup.

Trigger & Actor

The authenticated user or an application client requests the current household.

Application API contract

  • GET /v1/household returns the current household for the authenticated user.
  • A successful response includes the household ID, name, and the user’s role.
  • If the authenticated user has no household, the route returns 404 household_not_found; this is the normal onboarding state, not a domain event.
  • An unauthenticated request is rejected or redirected to Google authentication without revealing household state.

Command / Input

This slice has no command in the model.

Trigger

Triggered by: authenticated user or API client requesting the current household.

Event(s) Emitted

This slice has no event in the model.

Read Model / View

  • View: Current Household built from events: "Household Created"
Field Type Source / Notes
householdId uuid from event Household Created
name string from event Household Created
rootManagerUserId uuid from event Household Created
role string Derived from household membership
  • Consumed by: household setup, dashboard, and other authenticated household experiences.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: read-after-write for the creating user; current membership and role must be authorization-consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

No invariants declared in the model.

  • The view is scoped to the authenticated user and never accepts a client-supplied user ID.
  • A user belongs to at most one household in MVP.
  • A missing household is represented by the API resource-not-found response; it does not append an event or create setup state.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Scenario: Existing household is returned

  • Given:
    • an authenticated user belongs to a household
  • When:
    • the user requests GET /v1/household
  • Then:
    • the current household and the user’s role are returned
    • no domain event is recorded

Scenario: New user is directed to setup

  • Given:
    • an authenticated user does not belong to a household
  • When:
    • the user requests GET /v1/household
  • Then:
    • the API returns 404 household_not_found
    • no household state or domain event is created
    • the application may present initial household setup

Scenario: Household data is not disclosed across users

  • Given:
    • an authenticated user belongs to household A
  • When:
    • the user requests the current household
  • Then:
    • only household A is considered
    • the response contains no other household’s data

Alternate & Error Flows

  • A missing or expired session is rejected or redirected to Google authentication without disclosing household membership.
  • A projection or persistence failure returns a recoverable error and never converts an unknown failure into 404 household_not_found.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: resolve the household from the authenticated principal and enforce the same household authorization rules used by HTTP, MCP, worker, and scheduled entry points.
  • PII & compliance: return only the household fields needed by the caller; do not expose provider credentials or unrelated member data.
  • Performance / SLA: ordinary authenticated read latency; no external provider call required.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on: Household Created.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: household setup, dashboard, budgets, and transactions use the current household identity as their scope.

Open Questions

None for MVP.
